rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test a foundational multimodal configuration to assess if combining RNA and image data improves performance. This tests the core hypothesis of multimodal value with minimal complexity (simple concatenation fusion, basic encoders). It clarifies whether multimodal approaches are worth further exploration before investing in more complex models.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, concat fusion) achieved 0.526 validation accuracy. This experiment tests changing fusion from 'concat' to 'weighted' while keeping other parameters identical, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It balances exploration (testing a different fusion method) and exploitation (building on the previous multimodal/singleprofile setup). This comparison directly addresses whether weighted fusion could improve performance, a key design choice with potential for significant impact.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~0.526 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile (a key design choice) with avgpool aggregation, which was not tested before. It clarifies whether multiprofile improves performance and isolates the effect of aggregation, balancing exploration of profile settings with exploitation of the successful encoder combination.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile setups with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_018) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.618). This experiment tests changing fusion from concat to weighted, isolating the effect of fusion method while keeping other parameters consistent. This clarifies whether weighted fusion improves performance in this context, balancing exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l while keeping other settings identical, isolating the effect of the image encoder's complexity. This is a critical exploration to determine if a more advanced image encoder could further improve performance, balancing exploitation of the current best setup with targeted exploration of key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile, weighted fusion, and avgpool aggregation achieve high accuracy (config_019: 0.639). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping pca_n2000 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion. It isolates the effect of aggregation method, which is critical for multimodal integration, and builds on the success of weighted fusion.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (while keeping aggregation and fusion unchanged) improves performance, isolating the impact of the RNA representation. This balances exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of a key design choice.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_031) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (instead of avgpool) with the same RNA/image encoders and weighted fusion could further improve performance. It clarifies the impact of aggregation method on model performance, a critical design choice, while building on the promising foundation of config_031.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder achieve high accuracy (config_033: 0.713). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l image encoder and avgpool aggregation, which could reveal if a more powerful image encoder improves performance. It isolates the effect of the image encoder while maintaining the high-performing RNA encoder and weighted fusion, balancing exploration of key components with minimal changes.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039: 0.724989) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether using the newer scgpt RNA encoder with the same transformer aggregation and weighted fusion could further improve performance. It clarifies if scgpt's capabilities surpass scvi_n200 in this setup, making it the final test to potentially break the current accuracy record.
